name: Full Leaden Collection Phial
summary: In Kharanos, Ozzie Togglevolt seeks a sample from Gnomeregan’s troggs. He hopes it will cure irradiated leper gnomes, or perhaps make a dangerously potent rum.

sections.title: A Toxic Brew
sections.body:
A lead lining shields the bearer from the volatile green fallout saturating Gnomeregan. High Tinker Mekkatorque’s advisors flooded the lower corridors with toxic radiation to stop the invading troggs. Instead, the disaster corrupted troggs and surviving gnomes into maddened, irradiated horrors.

Irradiated Invaders and Pillagers leave fluid residue for refugee tinkerers in Kharanos. Ozzie Togglevolt and Razzle Sprysprocket use it as raw material in their experiments on remedies.

sections.title: Cure or Concoction
sections.body: Ozzie Togglevolt experiments frantically to address the fallout, while Gnoarn remains fixed on reclaiming the city. Ozzie hopes the liquid will treat an entrapped leper gnome and perhaps reverse his own baldness. In gnome laboratories, the line between a miraculous antidote and a highly volatile beverage remains dangerously thin.

faq.q: Why is the phial made of lead?
faq.answer: The phial’s lead lining shields its bearer from intense radioactive fallout gathered from Gnomeregan’s contaminated troggs. That lets them carry it back to Kharanos without sickness or death.
Ozzie Togglevolt, a gnome researcher in Kharanos, wants the irradiated fallout to experiment on a cure for leprosy-afflicted gnomes. Razzle Sprysprocket helps him.

faq.q: Where does the radiation in the phial come from?
faq.answer: The glowing green residue comes from Irradiated Invaders and Irradiated Pillagers, troggs prowling the tainted corridors leading into Gnomeregan.

faq.q: Does Ozzie actually cure the leper gnomes with it?
faq.answer: Ozzie’s experiments are chaotic and uncertain. His concoction aims to cure a captured leper gnome and restore his own hair, but gnome science often needs repeated testing and refined samples to find safe, consistent results.

angles.text: For exiled gnomes in Dun Morogh, carrying this toxic sample recalls the disaster that poisoned their ancestral home. It offers desperate hope of restoring their corrupted kin.
The lead casing reflects gnome safety protocols for handling volatile, toxic fallout in laboratory testing.
